adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 | An unauthenticated GET with any crafted embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job that creates a brand-new public topic, so distinct query strings on the allowed host give an attacker unlimited unthrottled topic/post creation. | adversarial | 100 |

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, if no existing embed is found it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` with the user possibly nil (`current_user.try(:id)`), and there is no authentication guard added in this diff. `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the Referer header is client-controlled and can be spoofed by a non-browser client.

The job path (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve`) will accept any `embed_url` whose host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and, if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` is false, it will fetch/import and create a new topic via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import`.

The throttling key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so an attacker can bypass the 60s throttle by varying the `embed_url` (e.g., different query strings/fragments) while keeping the host the same, resulting in effectively unlimited topic/post creation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 | `url` is interpolated into `<a href='#{url}'>` with no escaping, so an attacker-supplied embed_url containing a quote (URI parses `https://host/p?x='/onmouseover='...` fine) injects attributes into a post that is later rendered raw. | adversarial | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents` is appended with HTML containing `#{url}` without escaping (`url` comes from RSS/remote fetch and only checked by `/^https?\:\/\//`, which does not exclude quotes). The resulting HTML is passed through `absolutize_urls`, which parses/serializes with Nokogiri but does not remove or escape injected attributes; it will preserve them if the quote breaks out of the `href` value. The post is then created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes attribute/script injection via a crafted URL a real, verifiable stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 | Feed HTML is CGI.unescapeHTML'd (actively un-escaping `<script>`) and imported with cook_method raw_html and no sanitizer, so a feed item body becomes stored XSS for every viewer. | adversarial | 100 |

In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item bodies are taken from `i.content`, then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is applied, which will convert escaped tags like `<script>` into real `<script>` tags. That `content` is passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post via `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any injected HTML/JS from the feed becomes stored XSS for viewers of the embed page (and potentially elsewhere the post is rendered). No sanitizer is applied in this path in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then setting `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`. The `Referer` header is not a trustworthy authentication/authorization signal because a direct client (e.g., curl or any script) can supply an arbitrary `Referer` value; with `Referer: https://<embeddable_host>/...` the check will pass even when the request is not actually coming from an embedded page. There is no additional cryptographic token or other server-side verification in this controller to prevent such spoofing. Therefore the finding describes a real weakness present in the diff (relying on attacker-controlled `Referer` for access control).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (`document.location.reload()`), which re-hits `best` and will enqueue yet another `RetrieveTopic` job as long as the embed never becomes available. adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 | A regular job synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed, bypassing PollFeed's `sidekiq_options retry: false` so a poison feed is re-downloaded and re-imported on every RetrieveTopic retry. | adversarial | 75 |

That means `Jobs::PollFeed` is not being run by Sidekiq as its own job, so its `sidekiq_options retry: false` will not apply. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve the code does a pre-check `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later may create the record via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` which does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 | `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that embed_url forever, and the key is claimed before any work so failed retrievals are throttled like successful ones. | adversarial | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` the code does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then, in a separate call, `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two Redis operations are not atomic. If the process crashes or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL, and subsequent calls will always see `setnx` fail and return `true` (treating it as “retrieved recently”) indefinitely for that `embed_url`. Also, the key is claimed before any retrieval work is done, so even a failed retrieval attempt will still trigger throttling for the duration (or forever in the crash-between-calls scenario).

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 | RetrieveTopic runs the entire hourly PollFeed synchronously inside a web-request-triggered job, bypassing PollFeed's own retry:false and re-polling the whole feed on every Sidekiq retry. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (i.e., inline), rather than enqueuing it as its own Sidekiq job. That means `PollFeed`'s `sidekiq_options retry: false` is not used at all for this execution path—any failures come from the surrounding job (e.g., `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) which will typically retry by default. On each retry (or any later invocation after the 60s per-URL throttle expires), `TopicRetriever` will again run `PollFeed`, which fetches and processes the entire configured feed (`poll_feed` opens `feed_polling_url` and iterates `rss.items`). This is a real reliability/performance concern introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 | The feed item loop has no per-item rescue, so one bad item (nil content, RecordNotUnique, PostCreator failure) aborts every remaining item and retry:false drops them until the next hour. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job iterates `rss.items.each` and directly does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item exception handling. If any item has `content` nil (raising `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`), or if `TopicEmbed.import` raises (e.g., DB errors like RecordNotUnique due to the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, or PostCreator failures), the exception will abort the entire loop and the job. Because `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, the failed run will not be retried, so remaining items in that run are skipped until the next scheduled execution (and if a particular bad item consistently raises, later items may never be processed). This is a concrete reliability issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 | `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` sets no open/read timeout, so an unresponsive feed host can hang a Sidekiq worker on connect indefinitely. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` using Ruby's open-uri without passing any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options. That is verifiably true from the diff and means the Sidekiq job can block on network I/O (connect/DNS/read) for an extended period, tying up a worker when the feed host is slow or unresponsive. adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 | `open(url)` in import_remote sets no open/read timeout, so a slow or hung embed host can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the job does a synchronous network fetch with `open(url).read` (via open-uri) and provides no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (nor any overall deadline/size limit). adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 | Network and feed-parse errors are unrescued and unlogged; with retry:false a single transient failure silently loses the whole hour's import. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without any rescue. `open` (open-uri) can raise network/timeout/HTTP errors and `SimpleRSS.parse` can raise parsing errors on malformed feeds. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a transient exception will cause that scheduled run to fail with no Sidekiq retry, so that hour’s import attempt is lost. (The exception will bubble out; whether it is “unlogged” depends on Sidekiq logging, but the lack of rescue + no retry is directly verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 | OpenURI::HTTPError / SocketError / Errno from the remote fetch are unrescued, so any 404, 500 or DNS failure fails RetrieveTopic and burns all 25 default Sidekiq retries. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) calls `open(url).read` without any rescue. `open-uri` can raise `OpenURI::HTTPError` (404/500), `SocketError` (DNS), `Errno::*` (connection refused, timeouts, etc.). This method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is executed by the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq job; that job does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures will bubble up and cause the job to error and be retried by Sidekiq’s default retry policy (commonly 25 retries).

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 | The 60s redis throttle key is written before the retrieval runs and never cleared on failure, so Sidekiq's first retry (~15-45s later) is throttled into a silent no-op. | reliability | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` is created via `$redis.setnx` and given a 60s TTL *before* `perform_retrieve` runs. If `perform_retrieve` (or its network/import work) raises and the Sidekiq job retries within that 60s window, the next `retrieve` call will hit `retrieved_recently? == true` and return early without calling `perform_retrieve`. That makes the retry effectively a silent no-op, and because no exception is raised on that retry, Sidekiq will consider the job successful and stop retrying. The key is not cleared on failure anywhere in this diff (only expires).

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 | `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is non-atomic; a crash or redis error between them leaves a TTL-less key that permanently blocks retrieval of that embed_url for non-staff. | reliability | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is called in a separate command. If the process crashes or Redis/network errors occur after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is applied, the key can be left without a TTL. Because subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail, `retrieved_recently?` will return true indefinitely, permanently blocking retrieval for that `embed_url` (unless `no_throttle` is used). This is a real reliability defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 | Anonymous unauthenticated requests enqueue a RetrieveTopic job per request with no enqueue-time URL validation or rate limit, letting crawlers flood the Sidekiq queue. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` (no authentication required; current_user may be nil). The only controller-side check is `params.require(:embed_url)` plus the referer-host check in ensure_embeddable; there is no validation that `embed_url` is a valid URL nor any enqueue-time throttling/deduping. Throttling exists only inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (Redis setnx/expire), which runs when the job executes, so a crawler can still generate many queued jobs before workers drop them. This matches the proposed reliability problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 | Raising InvalidParameters for a missing embed_url makes Sidekiq retry a permanently unsatisfiable poison job 25 times before dead-lettering it. | reliability | 75 |

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 | A missing or misconfigured embed_by_username user makes the job return successfully with no log, leaving the client stuck in the endless reload loop. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, the code looks up the posting user via `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then silently `return if user.blank?`. adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26 | Same silent no-op when embed_by_username resolves to no user: the hourly job reports success while importing nothing. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 | Every feed item is imported with no per-run cap, so run time and DB write volume are unbounded for a large feed. | reliability | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no limit, paging, or cutoff. The number of items in `rss.items` is entirely determined by the remote feed, so the job’s runtime (and at least DB reads per item, and potentially DB writes if new/changed) can grow without bound for large feeds. adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:11 | The hourly recurrence has no overlap guard, so a slow poll (no timeouts, unbounded items) can run concurrently with the next tick and race on the unique embed_url index. | reliability | 50 |

adjudication.rationale: The new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` runs `recurrence { hourly }` and has no in-job lock/guard to prevent concurrent executions (e.g., long-running run overlapping the next scheduled run, or multiple Sidekiq processes/nodes). The job performs `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no explicit timeouts and then iterates all `rss.items` (potentially unbounded), so it can plausibly run longer than an hour. Concurrency can cause a real race in `TopicEmbed.import`: it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then, if blank, `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` while a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` was added. Two concurrent runs can both see `embed.blank?` and then one will raise a unique-constraint error, crashing the job. This is a verifiable reliability defect introduced by the diff (no locking + non-atomic check-then-create against a unique index).

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/models/topic_embed.rb:27 | When PostCreator fails the item is skipped without creating a TopicEmbed and without any log, so the import failure is invisible. | reliability | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when no existing embed is found it runs a transaction, calls `PostCreator.new(...).create`, and only creates the `TopicEmbed` row if `post.present?`. If `PostCreator#create` fails and returns nil/blank (e.g., validation failure despite `skip_validations: true`, or other internal failure modes that don’t raise), the method silently does nothing: no `TopicEmbed` is created and there is no logging or error reporting in this method. This makes the import failure effectively invisible and also means future retrieval attempts will keep retrying because `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).exists?` will remain false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 | No null check on `#discourse-comments`; if the container is absent or the script runs before it, `appendChild` throws and the embed silently never loads. | reliability | 100 |

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 | `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to the 'loading' render too, so a shared cache can keep serving the loading page after the topic already exists. | reliability | 50 |

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P0 | app/models/post.rb:133 | Post#cook returns the raw string verbatim for cook_method raw_html, bypassing the PrettyText/sanitize pipeline so third-party HTML (feed items, scraped pages) is stored in `cooked` and rendered as live markup. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new cook_method enum with :raw_html and changes Post#cook to `return raw` when that method is set, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). TopicEmbed.import uses this for RSS/scraped content (`PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`), and the embed view renders it as live markup (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`). Since the imported `contents` comes from external sources (SimpleRSS/open-uri and ruby-readability/open-uri), this introduces a verifiable XSS risk where third-party HTML can be stored and rendered unsanitized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 | RSS/Atom item content is CGI.unescapeHTML'd and imported with no sanitization at all, so anything in the feed (including <script>) becomes executable HTML on the forum origin. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces feed importing in `Jobs::PollFeed`, where `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` directly, explicitly skipping the rendering/sanitization pipeline. That means any HTML from the feed (including `<script>` or event-handler attributes) can be stored and later rendered; the embed view even does `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no sanitization step in this path, so this is a real XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 | The embed/feed URL is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted href attribute, so an embed_url containing a quote (accepted by URI and by the host check) breaks out and injects event-handler attributes into the stored raw HTML. | security | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML to `contents` using `"#{url}"` without any escaping. The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows quotes and other characters in the remainder of the string. A crafted URL like `http://eviltrout.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)` would pass the regex (and can still have host `eviltrout.com` when parsed elsewhere), break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute, and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML into the stored post. This is amplified by the new `cook_method :raw_html` path: `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for imported posts, so the injected HTML is rendered without sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 | The public embed page renders `raw post.cooked`, which for raw_html-cooked posts is unsanitized remote HTML served from the Discourse origin. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook mode where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), explicitly bypassing the normal rendering/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` from RSS/remote content (`SimpleRSS` content and `Readability::Document#content`). Then `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which for these posts is effectively untrusted remote HTML emitted verbatim from the Discourse origin. This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 | Access control for this public endpoint rests entirely on the Referer header, which any non-browser client can spoof, so the embeddable_host restriction is not an authorization boundary. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is allowed solely by checking `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then setting `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`. The `Referer` header is client-controlled and can be trivially spoofed by non-browser clients (or stripped/modified by some intermediaries), so this check is not a robust authorization boundary for the public `GET /embed/best` endpoint. A caller can supply any `Referer` header matching the configured host and bypass the intended restriction.

| P2 | app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 | An unauthenticated request (only a forged Referer needed) enqueues a job that makes the server fetch a remote URL and create a topic/post as embed_by_username; the throttle key is per-URL, so varying the query string bypasses it entirely. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController#best` does not require authentication and, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, it unconditionally `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` (even for `current_user == nil`). The only gate is `ensure_embeddable`, which trusts `request.referer` and only checks its host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; a client can send a forged Referer header matching that host. The queued `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which will fetch content via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` using `open(url).read` and create/update a topic/post as `SiteSetting.embed_by_username`. The throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` keys on the full `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying query strings (or other URL variations) trivially bypasses throttling and, because `topic_embeds.embed_url` is unique, also leads to many distinct topics/posts being created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 | import_remote fetches a user-influenced URL with open-uri before any scheme check, and the embeddable_host allowlist in TopicRetriever is not re-applied after open-uri follows redirects, enabling SSRF to internal hosts/ports. | security | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` on a URL ultimately derived from `params[:embed_url]` (via `EmbedController#best` -> `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks the *initial* `@embed_url` host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `open-uri` will follow HTTP redirects by default and the code does not re-validate the final destination host/port after redirects. That allows a URL on the allowed host to redirect to an internal host/port (SSRF) and be fetched server-side. There is also no explicit scheme restriction in `import_remote` itself beyond what `invalid_host?` implies for the initial URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 | Kernel#open is called on the feed_polling_url site setting with no scheme validation, so a value beginning with "|" executes a shell command as the Sidekiq user. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Ruby’s `Kernel#open` treats strings beginning with `"|"` as a command to execute (opens a pipe), and there is no validation/whitelisting of `feed_polling_url` to ensure it’s an `http(s)` URL. Therefore a maliciously set `feed_polling_url` like `"|id"` could execute a shell command when the scheduled Sidekiq job runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 | The postMessage handler validates the sender with a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of an exact origin comparison. | security | 100 |

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the message handler does `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring containment check rather than verifying the sender’s origin exactly matches the expected Discourse origin. Substring checks can produce false positives when `e.origin` is contained within `discourseUrl` but is not the same origin (e.g., differing host/port or a crafted `discourseUrl` that contains another origin as a prefix). A strict origin comparison against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` would be the correct pattern for postMessage validation.
